openings.claim: Unreliable storage addresses may cause second searches: stale exception entries after moves and household-surname misfiling are distinct candidates. Test current locators tied to reservation identity while retaining surname shelves, dividers and cart. Fast synthetic cart pickups challenge mandatory shelving as a speed improvement.
openings.discriminator: Separate stale-entry searches from household-mismatch searches. If verified locations and identities leave delays concentrated in peak demand with little searching, clerk occupancy rivals address unreliability. If current entries leave mismatch-associated searches unchanged, slip updates alone fail. Match cart comparisons by arrival volume and book size.
openings.probe: The existing evening clerk records arrival, service start, retrieval, completion, freshness, mismatches, second searches and wrong-reader handoffs on existing behind-desk paper. Compare comparable pickups with move-time locator updates. Verify recipients. Use only two shelves and one cart; keep names and contacts behind the desk. Count preparation and later corrections toward ten daily clerk-minutes; stop added preparation at the cap.
openings.uncertainty: Fit applies only to the capped probe. Existing identity-checking and mismatch-observation capabilities are unconfirmed. Eight preparation minutes plus six correction minutes establish no spare capacity. Household mismatches explaining second searches, cart volume/size effects and interview representativeness remain unknown. All evidence is synthetic; cap-limited trials are inconclusive.

decision: Run the bounded diagnostic comparison if existing hold information supports observation. Require at least 95% of available pickups within two minutes and no wrong-reader handoffs before claiming success. No staffing or furniture additions. Locator benefit, sustained feasibility and target attainment remain unproved; reader uncertainty about hold presence is an additional untested concern.
